results.title: What is going wrong in Tamil Nadu’s SIR? | Focus Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
results.label: yes
results.reason: elections_process/state: Issues in Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process for voter rolls.

notes.subject: polity
notes.why_in_news: The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Tamil Nadu is facing operational failures, potentially leading to the mass deletion of genuine voters before the 2026 elections.
notes.fact_box: The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a periodic exercise by the Election Commission of India (ECI) to update and clean voter rolls. In Tamil Nadu, the process is currently criticized for unrealistic deadlines, confusing forms, and lack of clear instructions to citizens.

prelims_pointers.text: Election Commission of India (ECI) is the constitutional body responsible for voter list maintenance and conducting elections.
The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a periodic exercise to ensure the accuracy of the electoral roll.
Tamil Nadu is the state where the current SIR operational issues were reported in November 2025.

notes.mains_question: Critically analyze the challenges in maintaining accurate electoral rolls and suggest measures to ensure inclusive voter participation during intensive revision cycles.
mains_dimensions: Administrative bottleneck: Unrealistic deadlines and lack of standardized instructions leading to procedural errors in voter deletion.
Inclusionary risk: Potential disenfranchisement of genuine voters due to complex form designs and poor public communication.
Technological gap: Need for robust digital verification to cross-reference identity data and prevent arbitrary deletions.
